Hi Tessa / Marcus,

Thanks again for the initial call last week. MediCore's CIO asked us to schedule a technical demo that includes our EU Data Protection Officer (Sophie Laurent) and our APAC security lead (Kaito Suzuki) — this will be for a potential dedicated/private deployment. Because of the cross‑region attendees we need to find a window that works across PST / CET / JST.

High-level asks:
- Live demo of the Dedicated flow and admin console (30–40 min)
- Deep dive on audit logs, KMS integration, and data retention (20 min)
- Time reserved for Sophie and Kaito to ask jurisdictional questions (15 min)

Could you propose 2–3 windows next week? Preferably avoid very late CET hours if possible. Sophie is in Paris (CET). Kaito is in Tokyo (JST).

I attached our updated security questionnaire (v2) — happy to fill anything you need in advance.

Best,
Anna

Hi Anna — thanks for the note and for attaching the questionnaire. We'll make sure Sophie and Kaito get the time they need.

Quick note on timezones / DST: the US fell back in early November so Pacific is currently UTC‑8. CET is UTC+1 (Paris) and JST is UTC+9 (Tokyo). That gives us an 17‑hour spread to juggle.

Proposed windows (all durations include Q&A):
- Option A (EU‑friendly): 09:30 PT / 18:30 CET / 02:30 JST (next day) — 75 min
- Option B (US‑morning compromise): 11:00 PT / 20:00 CET / 04:00 JST (next day) — 75 min
- Option C (APAC‑leaning): 16:00 PT / 01:00 CET (next day) / 09:00 JST (next day) — 75 min

Option A keeps Sophie in regular evening hours but pushes Kaito very late; Option C flips that. Option B is middle‑of‑the‑road but requires both ends to be outside normal business hours.

Marcus / Naomi — can you check internal availability and whether we can bring a Redwood security engineer (I suggest Naomi) and an SRE product lead for the KV cache / network routing questions?

I attached an .ics with the three proposed slots to make it easier for mediCore to tentatively block.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

- Naomi, if you're available, which of the three slots is least painful for you? (I prefer Option B personally.)
